# Heroes

> Heroes is a small compiled programming language designed to catch common
> mistakes in code generated by language models. It has no null, exceptions or
> implicit numeric conversions. Programs can use C libraries, and clang checks
> their declarations against the library headers. The compiler is written in
> Heroes and reproduces the C file from which it was built.

Read the specification before writing Heroes code. It defines the complete
language and stays below 4096 tokens, leaving room in the prompt for the program.
A test checks this limit on every commit.

- [Specification as text](https://heroes-lang.org/spec.md): the complete file to include in a prompt.
- [Specification page](https://heroes-lang.org/spec/): the same text, with an explanation of the size limit.

The repository is open to read, under the Apache 2.0 licence. The language is
in beta: before version 1.0.0 a change in the middle number can change the
language itself, and a change in the last number never does.

Rules to follow when generating code: use four spaces for indentation, never
tabs; name arguments when two parameters share a type; handle every variant
case in `match`, without a catch-all `_` branch; represent fallible results as
`T?` and handle or propagate errors explicitly. Use `???` for an unfinished
expression. The compiler reports its expected type and checks the surrounding
code, but produces no executable while holes remain.

## Pages

- [Home](https://heroes-lang.org/): an introduction, code examples and the project's hypothesis.
- [Examples](https://heroes-lang.org/examples/): source code, commands and recorded output where available. `/examples/index.json` provides the same collection as data, with a hash for each file.
- [Start](https://heroes-lang.org/start/): how to build the compiler, find its runtime and run a program.
- [Why Heroes](https://heroes-lang.org/why/): why the language uses explicit syntax and C libraries, what has been measured and what remains to be tested.
- [The project](https://heroes-lang.org/project/): how to verify that the compiler reproduces its own C, how changes are reviewed and the principles printed by `heroes this`.
- [The author](https://heroes-lang.org/about/): Giuseppe Arici, CTO at Codermine in Brescia and author of *Heroes of code*, a history of programming languages told as a dream journey with David Bowie. The book is published on Amazon. Arici had never written a compiler before Heroes.
- [Development log](https://heroes-lang.org/log/): project changes and review findings, newest first.
- [Thanks](https://heroes-lang.org/about/thanks/): the language designers and researchers whose work influenced Heroes, with each contribution.
- [Documentation](https://heroes-lang.org/docs/): chapters explaining values, functions, errors, loops, modules and C libraries, with code checked against repository files.
- [Errors](https://heroes-lang.org/docs/errors/): compiler messages, automatic fixes marked `certain` and measured detection rates for different kinds of mistake.

Each page also has an Italian version under `/it/`, linked through the language
switch and `hreflang` metadata. Both versions preserve the same code, compiler
output and twenty principles printed by `heroes this`.

## Source

- [Repository](https://github.com/heroes-lang/heroes): the compiler, specification and design records. Clone it, build with `clang -I runtime seed/heroes.c runtime/runtime.c -o heroes`, then run `./heroes run examples/gallery/00-first.hero`. Issues are welcome; code contributions are not open yet, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` names the conditions that have to be met first.
- [Example programs](https://heroes-lang.org/examples/): read directly from `examples/` when the site is built.

## Notes

- There is no installer yet, so the compiler is built from source with one
  clang command. The current compiler is written in Heroes; the earlier
  compiler is archived and no longer builds.
- `heroes check --json` emits schema 1 with stable snake_case error codes,
  source locations, notes and suggested fixes.
